data.title: Rock Tech Lithium upsizes private placement to C$6M with strategic backing
data.description:
Key points:
  • Rock Tech Lithium said on Tuesday that it increased its previously announced non-brokerage private placement to up to C$6M.
  • The company has so far issued 8.17M units for about C$5.31M, including C$3.51M raised in the latest tranche.
  • A strategic investor subscribed to C$3.25M and is expected to enter a strategic equity partnership tied to Rock Tech’s fully permitted Guben lithium hydroxide converter in Germany.
  • Each unit is priced at C$0.65 and includes one common share and half a warrant. Each full warrant allows the holder to buy one additional share at C$0.90 for 36 months.
  • The proceeds will be used to advance the Georgia Lake Mine feasibility study, develop its Red Rock Converter in Ontario, and support general working capital.
  • Separately, the company also appointed Derek Sobel as CFO, replacing Christopher Wright, who is relocating to Australia.
  • The financing remains subject to final TSX Venture Exchange approval.

data.title: US House committee recommends contempt of Congress for Leon Black in Epstein probe
data.description:
By Isla Binnie and Nolan D. McCaskill

The U.S. House of Representatives Oversight Committee voted to recommend holding Leon Black in contempt of Congress on Tuesday, after the Wall Street billionaire declined to comply with subpoenas as part of a probe into the activities of late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

Black, who co-founded private equity giant Apollo Global Management , ⁠is among several prominent political and business figures who have been called to testify about their ties to the late financier.

The 41-0 committee vote sets up a vote by the full House to refer the case to the Justice Department for possible prosecution under a simple majority threshold. Contempt of Congress is a misdemeanor charge that carries up to a year in prison and a fine of up to $100,000.

Black gave up his role as Apollo chief executive in 2021 after an external law firm found he had paid Epstein $158 million for tax and estate planning.

He sued the committee this month and declined to appear at a deposition. The deposition was scheduled after a voluntary appearance in June during which Black told the committee he never abused women or engaged in sex trafficking and had never had sex with underage women. He denies knowledge of Epstein's conduct.

He walked out during the June interview, according to members of the committee, who ordered him to ⁠come back ​to testify under oath and then issued subpoenas for documents.

Black's lawyers said on Tuesday the contempt resolution showed the committee had "lost sight of its legislative purpose and (was) abusing its power", adding they had written to ask the Office of Congressional Conduct to investigate Comer.

Epstein was found dead in a New York ‌City ⁠jail cell in 2019, and his death was ruled a suicide.

data.title: S&P 500, Nasdaq, Dow End Lower As Investors Price In Rate Hike Ahead Of Fed Meeting — AMZN, META, MU, TSLA, PLTR In Focus
data.description:
Key points:
  • The S&P 500 ended Tuesday 0.5% lower, while the Nasdaq 100 slipped 0.7% and the Dow Jones Industrial Average eased 0.6%.
  • Benchmark 10-year yields hit 5%, the highest level in nearly two decades.
  • Meta plans to begin deploying an in-house AI chip in data centers by next year.

U.S. stock indices fell on Tuesday as Treasury yields spiked to multi-year highs, with investors pricing in a Federal Reserve rate hike at its interest rate meeting on Wednesday.

The S&P 500 ended Tuesday 0.5% lower, while the Nasdaq 100 slipped 0.7% and the Dow Jones Industrial Average eased 0.6%. The Russell 2000, which tracks stocks with small market capitalizations, fell about 0.8%.

Among ETFs tracking benchmark indexes, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY) fell 0.4%, and Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) ended Tuesday 0.6% lower, while the SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF Trust (DIA) was down 0.5%.

Meanwhile, the VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH) added 0.2%, while the iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) dropped 0.6%, tracking weakness in Advanced Micro Devices (AMD), Nvidia (NVDA) and Micron Tech (MU). The broader Vanguard Information Technology ETF (VGT) ended 0.2% lower.

Retail sentiment on Stocktwits for QQQ, SPY, and DIA was ‘bearish,’ with ‘high’ message volumes.

US Market Drivers

IndexMoveClose
Dow Jones Industrial Average-0.6%52,093.11
S&P 500-0.5%7,585.73
Nasdaq 100-0.7%28,937.84

Benchmark 10-year Treasury yields touched 5.041% on Tuesday, climbing to their peak since 2007. The 10-year rate subsequently pulled back from session highs, recently trading up over 3 basis points around 5%. The iShares 20+ Year Treasury ETF (TLT) eased 0.3%.

Moreover, global crude prices extended gains on Tuesday, with Brent crude oil futures rising almost 3% to end the session at $108.75 a barrel, while WTI futures advanced more than 4% to $105.83.

As oil and yields continue to spike, investor attention this week will remain focused on the Federal Reserve’s September policy meeting announcement due on Wednesday. Fed funds futures traders are pricing in a roughly 92% likelihood of a rate hike, according to CME’s FedWatch tool.

“The debate has shifted from ‘if’ to ‘how much’ tightening this cycle will require to restore price stability,” Seema Shah at Principal Asset Management told Bloomberg. “A one-and-done hiking approach is unlikely.”

Key Trending Stocks

Amazon (AMZN): Amazon Web Services (AWS) has suffered permanent data loss at several of its Middle Eastern server facilities as a direct result of the ongoing US-Iran conflict.

Meta Platforms (META): The company is reportedly planning to launch its next-generation in-house artificial intelligence chips in the first half of 2027

Micron Technology (MU): The company announced it had demonstrated the first 512GB DDR5 registered dual in-line memory module (RDIMM) across multiple server platforms.

Tesla (TSLA): U.S. auto safety regulator pressed the company for more details on its dedicated robotaxi offering

Palantir Technologies (PLTR): The cybersecurity firm looks relatively cheap compared with AI-linked software peers, according to UBS, which expects the stock to rebound as demand for its artificial intelligence-linked software services gains traction.

data.title: Microsoft announces quarterly dividend increase
data.description:
Annual shareholders meeting set for Dec. 8, 2026

REDMOND, Wash., Sept. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Microsoft Corp. on Tuesday announced that its board of directors declared a quarterly dividend of $0.98 per share, reflecting a 7 cent or 8% increase over the previous quarter's dividend. The dividend is payable Dec. 10, 2026, to shareholders of record on Nov. 19, 2026. The ex-dividend date will be Nov. 19, 2026.

In addition, the company announced the 2026 Annual Shareholders Meeting will be held Dec. 8, 2026. Shareholders at the close of business on Sept. 30, 2026, the record date, will be entitled to vote their shares.

This year's annual shareholders meeting will be held virtually and hosted by Satya Nadella, chairman and chief executive officer; Amy Hood, executive vice president and chief financial officer; Brad Smith, vice chair and president; and Sandra E. Peterson, Microsoft lead independent director.

About Microsoft

Microsoft (Nasdaq "MSFT" @microsoft) creates platforms and tools powered by AI to deliver innovative solutions that meet the evolving needs of our customers. The technology company is committed to making AI available broadly and doing so responsibly, with a mission to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more.

data.title: Inside OpenAI's Ad Rush — WSJ
data.description:
By Suzanne Vranica

OpenAI Chief Executive Sam Altman once called the combination of ads and artificial intelligence "uniquely unsettling." Now his company is building a sprawling advertising business, at breakneck speed.

It is trying to establish a revenue stream to sustain its free ChatGPT tier and help offset soaring computing costs ahead of its planned initial public offering. In a milestone for the fledgling operation, the company said last month it was on pace to hit $1 billion in annualized ad revenue. But standing up an ad business so quickly has produced mixed results and, some advertisers say, administrative headaches and operational glitches.

OpenAI has taken an "everything, everywhere, all at once" approach to its ad rollout, said NewStreet Research analyst Dan Salmon, calling the pace impressive and unprecedented.

OpenAI started testing ads with some U.S.-based ChatGPT users in February, adding a labeled box featuring a relevant brand below the AI-generated answer. It is introducing tools for advertisers rapidly-to attract Fortune 500 companies but also the small and medium businesses that provide the bulk of ad revenue for Meta Platforms.

"This is one of the fastest ad builds in history, from my experience," said Dave Dugan, OpenAI's head of global ads solutions.

Seven months in, the ad business is now in more than 50 countries. Still, it isn't growing as fast as some industry analysts wanted to see. NewStreet Research recently cut its revenue forecast for the ads business, citing the $1 billion figure.

New ad businesses often experience growing pains. Netflix, which is still growing its ad business, faced early complaints that the subscriber base for its ad tier was too small and advertisers couldn't effectively target specific groups. And advertisers questioned whether Facebook's ad business delivered a good return ahead of its IPO.

Rocket Chief Marketing Officer Jonathan Mildenhall described the performance of his company's OpenAI ads so far as "underwhelming," saying he didn't see any material impact from its testing. Before increasing ad spending, Mildenhall wants better targeting and a smoother transition between chats and ad content.

OpenAI's foray into advertising got off to a bumpy start, initially charging some large brands a steep rate of about $60 per 1,000 views whether or not users clicked. That is a far cry from other digital ad businesses that offer highly targeted ads that brands only pay for when users click through. OpenAI's rates have since fallen significantly, as the company moved to auction-based pricing.

In those early days, it limited how many ads it showed users to monitor whether sponsored content negatively affected the ChatGPT experience. Some brands struggled to spend their allocated budgets because ad opportunities were limited, leading some to pause their participation until the product suite becomes more stable, advertisers said.

"We started with a total focus on user trust," OpenAI's Dugan said, adding that the company is in a different place now that the ad operation has matured.

The company has recruited a string of Meta alums for ad leadership, sales and product engineering roles, including Dugan. It is using its own Codex AI tool to quickly churn out updates and new features.

Three months into the venture, OpenAI introduced its tool that helps track the purchase activity of users who clicked on ads to prove they worked. It took Facebook about a dozen years to do that, Salmon said.

Some brands have been hesitant to deploy the trackers on their sites given the sensitivity around AI and privacy, ad buyers said.

OpenAI's newer ad products are now beginning to resemble some of those offered by Google, Meta and Amazon, including pay-per-click formats and carousels that show multiple products.

It is also experimenting with an ad format that launches a customized ChatGPT conversation when clicked, answering specific questions regarding the advertised product, ad buyers said.

OpenAI introduced a self-serve platform in May that allows companies to upload creative materials, set budgets and track performance-an offering that helps attract small and midsize businesses that can't afford major advertising firms. Ad buyers said the platform wasn't as sophisticated as Google's and Meta's but had still proved effective.

ChatGPT has more than one billion weekly active users, and advertisers say they can't afford to sit on the sidelines as AI changes how people search for information and make buying decisions.

But OpenAI's back-end infrastructure has at times struggled to keep up with demand and some ad executives said the system remains buggy.

Earlier this year, Tamara Rosenthal, the head of marketing at Taskrabbit, was surprised to see thousands of dollars in unfamiliar charges on her company credit card. "I'm being hacked by OpenAI," she recalled telling her accounting department. Her team explained that they had begun testing ads on OpenAI.

Not qualifying for invoicing didn't stop Taskrabbit, which was eager to test the service. "That's how desperate marketers are to get on there," Rosenthal said.

Before expanding its investment, Taskrabbit said it needs better ad-targeting options and more information about how people search on the platform.

Hungryroot CMO Adam Weber said early results were encouraging and he was optimistic about ChatGPT ads because chatbot queries can be more detailed than regular searches, allowing for more personalized ads.

"Even though there's been hiccups, brands can't afford to not test and learn here," said Spencer Lian-Thornton, a vice president at marketing firm Mindgruve. "Ignoring this today is like saying buying stuff online will never catch on."

Write to Suzanne Vranica at Suzanne.Vranica@wsj.com

data.title: Lenovo inks MOU with MemryX to expand sovereign edge AI in Saudi Arabia
data.description:
Lenovo signed a memorandum of understanding with MemryX, a provider of power-efficient, scalable AI technology, to expand the deployment of sovereign edge AI solutions in Saudi Arabia.

The agreement builds on joint platform deployments already operating in the country and establishes a framework for Lenovo and MemryX to pursue additional opportunities across infrastructure, industrial operations, smart cities and video management. The collaboration also supports Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030 by enabling organizations to deploy practical AI capabilities while maintaining greater control over their data and computing infrastructure.

The joint platform combines the Lenovo ThinkEdge SE455 V3 rugged edge server with the MemryX Cascade 100P AI accelerator to process video and sensor data on site.

"What matters to customers is being able to do that while keeping their data close to where it's created and under their control," said Salman Faqeeh, Vice President and General Manager, Saudi Arabia, Lenovo. "That's why our work with MemryX is relevant and timely. Together, we're helping bring AI into real-world environments where it can make an immediate difference. What's even more relevant is that this isn't a future concept. We're already seeing this deployment help customers improve safety and efficiency in real operating environments across Saudi Arabia."
